newsitem.title: ITALY: Michael Jackson testifies in Italy plagiarism suit.
newsitem.headline: Michael Jackson testifies in Italy plagiarism suit.

text.p: Pop star Michael Jackson made a lightning trip to Rome on Tuesday to answer allegations of plagiarism in a lawsuit brought by an Italian singer.

The American performer spoke for about 75 minutes in court in the city's huge justice complex, denying accusations that he copied the song "Will You Be There" in his 1991 "Dangerous" album from a composition by the Italian, Al Bano.
Jackson had arrived from Paris on a private flight in time to testify and was scheduled to return immediately to the French capital, bringing his entire stay in Rome to about four hours.
"I have never taken or stolen anything in my life," Jackson said. "These accusations...are totally false."
His unexpected appearance was noticed by court employees who saw him enter the building with an entourage of guards.
By the time he left, a big crowd of journalists, fans and bystanders had gathered outside.
About a dozen Italian police officers and several private security guards surrounded Jackson as he left the courtroom. He waved briefly but made no comment.
Jackson wore black pants, a burgandy shirt, a black military-style overcoat with a police badge on one arm and his signature wide-brimmed hat.
Bano accused Jackson in 1992 of plagiarising his 1987 song "I Cigni di Balaka" (The Swans of Balaka), which he says he wrote to honour the late Indian poet Rabindranath Tagore.
Bano, a popular singer in Italy, is married to Romina Power, the daughter of the late actor Tyrone Power.
Jackson testified that he had never met Bano and had never heard of his song until faced with the lawsuit.
